houthis.definition: An armed political movement from northern Yemen, formally called Ansar Allah. It has controlled Yemen's capital, Sanaa, since 2014, is aligned with Iran, and fought a Saudi-led military coalition from 2015.

irgc.definition: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, a military force set up after the 1979 revolution to protect the Islamic Republic. It is separate from Iran's regular army and has its own ground forces, navy, air force and an overseas arm, the Quds Force.

strait-of-hormuz.definition: The narrow sea passage between Iran and Oman that links the Persian Gulf to the open ocean. In normal times roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes through it, so closing it pushes up energy prices around the world.

kremlin.definition: The fortress in central Moscow that holds the Russian president's offices. News reports use the word as shorthand for the Russian government.

fii.definition: Saudi Arabia's yearly investor conference in Riyadh. It's nicknamed 'Davos in the Desert' after the World Economic Forum's meeting in Davos, Switzerland.

yellow-vests.definition: The gilets jaunes, a French protest movement that began in 2018 over fuel taxes and the cost of living. It's named after the high-visibility vests French drivers must carry.

bond-yield.definition: The return investors demand for lending money to a government. When yields rise, borrowing costs the government more, usually because investors see more risk in its finances.

paris-agreement.definition: The 2015 global climate deal. Countries agreed to keep warming well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels and to try to limit it to 1.5°C, with each country setting its own emissions pledges.

cop31.definition: The 31st UN climate change conference, where almost every country meets to negotiate climate action. COP31 takes place in Turkey in November 2026.

unep.definition: The United Nations Environment Programme. Each year it publishes a report measuring the gap between countries' emissions pledges and what's needed to meet the Paris Agreement goals.

ebola-bundibugyo.definition: One of the species of Ebola virus, first identified in Uganda's Bundibugyo district in 2007. Unlike the more common Zaire species, it has no approved vaccine or specific treatment.

rsf.definition: The Rapid Support Forces, a Sudanese paramilitary force that grew out of the Janjaweed militias of Darfur. It has been at war with Sudan's army for control of the country since April 2023.

abyei.definition: A small, oil-producing area on the border between Sudan and South Sudan that both countries claim. Its status was left unresolved when South Sudan became independent in 2011, and UN peacekeepers are based there.

tigray.definition: A region in northern Ethiopia. A war between Ethiopia's federal government and Tigrayan forces from 2020 to 2022 killed hundreds of thousands of people before a peace deal was signed in Pretoria.

fdlr.definition: The Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda, an armed group in eastern DR Congo. It was founded by Rwandan Hutu fighters, including people linked to the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi.

sir.definition: An exercise by India's Election Commission to re-check voter rolls house by house and remove duplicate, dead or relocated voters. It started as a pilot in Bihar in 2025 and has since run in phases across the country.

midterms.definition: US elections held halfway through a president's four-year term, for all 435 House seats, about a third of the Senate and many state offices. The 2026 midterms are on 3 November.

super-pac.definition: A US political committee that can raise and spend unlimited money for or against candidates, as long as it doesn't coordinate directly with their campaigns.

west-bank.definition: Palestinian territory between Israel and Jordan that Israel has occupied since 1967. About three million Palestinians and several hundred thousand Israeli settlers live there, and most countries consider the settlements illegal under international law.

triple-lock.definition: Ireland's rule that it sends more than a small number of troops abroad only with a UN mandate, government approval and a vote in the Dáil, its parliament. It's tied to Ireland's tradition of military neutrality.

patriots-for-europe.definition: A far-right group in the European Parliament formed in 2024. Its members include Hungary's Fidesz and France's National Rally.

cambridge-analytica.definition: A British political consulting firm that, it was revealed in 2018, had harvested data from up to 87 million Facebook users without their consent. The scandal led to fines and lawsuits against Facebook, now Meta.

php.definition: A programming language that runs on web servers. It powers a large share of the web, including sites built on WordPress.

chapter-11.definition: The part of US bankruptcy law that lets a company keep operating while it reorganizes its debts under a court's supervision, instead of shutting down.

737-max.definition: Boeing's newest family of 737 jets. Two fatal crashes in 2018 and 2019 grounded the plane worldwide for about 20 months and delayed later versions such as the Max 10.

kelvin-wave.definition: A huge, slow wave that travels beneath the ocean surface along the equator or a coastline, carrying warm water with it. Kelvin waves help start and strengthen El Niño.

el-nino.definition: A natural climate pattern in which the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean warms up every few years. It shifts weather around the world and usually nudges global temperatures up.

psilocybin.definition: The compound in 'magic mushrooms' that causes psychedelic effects. Researchers are testing it as a treatment for conditions including depression.

imf.definition: The International Monetary Fund, a global institution, owned by most of the world's governments, that lends to governments in financial trouble and publishes forecasts for the world economy.

ocha.definition: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, which organises the UN's emergency aid and reports on crises such as wars and disasters.

sakharov-prize.definition: The European Union's top human rights award, given each year since 1988 by the European Parliament. It is named after Andrei Sakharov, a Soviet scientist and dissident.

icc.definition: A court in The Hague, opened in 2002, that tries individuals for genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity and aggression when national courts cannot or will not. The US, Russia, China and Israel are not members.

gang-suppression-force.definition: An international security force approved by the UN Security Council in 2025 to help Haiti's police fight the armed gangs that control much of Port-au-Prince.

starshield.definition: A military version of SpaceX's Starlink satellite internet service, developed for the US Department of Defense.

class-action.definition: A lawsuit brought by a few people on behalf of a larger group who say they were harmed in the same way, so that all their claims are decided together.

epic-fury.definition: The name of the joint Israeli-American military operation that began the war with Iran at the end of February 2026.

national-rally.definition: France's main far-right party, led by Marine Le Pen. It holds its annual congress in Orléans this weekend.

knesset.definition: Israel's parliament, which has 120 seats. A coalition needs at least 61 of them to govern.

plenum.definition: A full meeting of the Chinese Communist Party's Central Committee, usually held behind closed doors, where major policy and personnel decisions are discussed.

frontex.definition: The European Union's border and coast guard agency, which helps member states control the EU's external borders and return migrants.

austrac.definition: Australia's financial intelligence agency, which supervises businesses such as casinos for money-laundering and terrorism-financing risks.

federal-reserve.definition: The central bank of the United States. It sets a key interest rate that influences borrowing costs across the economy and, through them, prices, jobs and the value of the dollar.

legislative-council.definition: The upper house of the legislature in some Indian states, such as Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. Its members, called MLCs, are chosen partly by elected legislators and partly by graduates, teachers and local bodies.

ndrf.definition: India's National Disaster Response Force, a specialist national unit that rescues people and gives relief during floods, cyclones, earthquakes and other disasters. Each state also has its own response force, the SDRF.
